memory_candidates.content: When a Neovim-config extension system has TWO independent deploy paths for the same logical file -- an install-once root-files copy AND a separate merge routine reading a differently-named merge-sources fragment -- always verify which path actually owns the target you are editing (check manifest.json's merge_targets.<key>.source vs. root-files/<same-basename>) before assuming an addition to one will ever reach an already-initialized repo. Adding new hook registrations only to the install-once file is a silent dead end: copy_root_files skips already-existing targets unconditionally, and the merge step for the SAME deployed filename can be reading a completely different source file that was never touched.

When adding a new hook command to a JSON merge-source fragment that will later be deep-merged into a live settings file via whole-matcher-object vim.deep_equal comparison, add it as its OWN dedicated single-command matcher object rather than appending the command into an existing shared matcher object. Object-level dedup only skips re-adding an object equal to one already merged in; appending a new command into an existing object changes that object's identity, so on the NEXT merge it will no longer match its previously-merged self and its sibling commands get re-registered as duplicates. A dedicated single-command object stays byte-identical across repeated merges and is therefore idempotent.
